oneLine: Persistent Systems crosses 90% ownership in Nagarro, executing a squeeze-out buyout of minority shareholders.

sources.title: Persistent to squeeze out existing Nagarro shareholders en route to become seventh-largest

synopsis: Persistent Systems has increased its stake in German software engineering firm Nagarro to 94%, crossing the 90% threshold required under German regulations to execute a squeeze-out buyout of remaining minority shareholders and merge Nagarro into a German subsidiary. The acquisition, valued at $1.3 billion with $1.1 billion paid for shares including a stake sale by Lantano, is partially funded by a €1.4 billion ($1.6 billion) loan from Barclays that must be repaid within 18 months. The transaction is expected to be completed by March next year, creating a combined entity with at least $2.7 billion in revenue and propelling Persistent to become the seventh-largest tech services firm in India.
